title: Green Curry Paste (Nam Prik Gaeng Kiew Wan)
description: Green Curry Paste (Nam Prik Gaeng Kiew Wan) is a classic Thai curry paste made with fresh green chilies, fragrant herbs, roasted spices, and shrimp paste. It is the foundation of authentic Thai green curry, offering a vibrant color, fresh aroma, and balanced heat.

ingredients.title: Fresh Aromatics
items: 10–12 fresh green Thai chilies (adjust to heat preference)
3–4 mild green chilies (like jalapeño or serrano, for color + volume)
1 tbsp chopped coriander root (or lower stems if root unavailable)
1 stalk lemongrass (tender inner part only), finely sliced
1 tbsp galangal, chopped (or ginger as a substitute)
1 tsp kaffir lime zest (or regular lime zest + pinch of fresh bay leaf)
1 tbsp Thai sweet basil leaves (optional, for a deeper herbal note)

ingredients.title: Seasoning
items: ½ tsp shrimp paste (or 1 tsp fermented soy bean paste/miso for vegetarian)

instruction.title: Method
steps:
1. Dry Toast Spices:
• Toast coriander, cumin, and white peppercorns in a dry skillet over medium heat until fragrant (1–2 minutes). Let cool and grind into powder.

2. Pound Fresh Ingredients:
• In a mortar and pestle (or blender), pound or blend green chilies, garlic, shallots, lemongrass, galangal, lime zest, and coriander root into a smooth paste.

3. Add Spices & Shrimp Paste:
• Incorporate ground spices and shrimp paste. Pound until fully blended and smooth, adding a splash of water or oil if needed for consistency.

servingSuggestions.title: Storage
items: Refrigerator: Airtight container, up to 1 week.
Freezer: Freeze in tablespoon portions (e.g., ice cube trays) for up to 3 months.
About ½ cup, suitable for 2–3 dishes.

chefTips: Use the freshest green chilies for the brightest color.
Thai sweet basil adds a deeper herbal aroma.
A mortar and pestle produces the most authentic texture.
Adjust the number of Thai chilies to control heat.
Freeze in small portions for convenient cooking.
